t: France built two colonial empires: one in North America and the Caribbean, lost in 1763, and a larger one in Africa and Asia.
Plantation slavery made Saint-Domingue the world's richest colony, while the later empire extracted raw materials for French industry.
Nationalist wars from Dien Bien Phu to Algeria ended it, leaving French as an official language in twenty-nine countries.
dyk: By the 1780s Saint-Domingue, now Haiti, produced around 40 per cent of Europe's sugar and some 60 per cent of its coffee.
ev: Jacques Cartier reaches the Gulf of St. Lawrence and claims land for Francis I
Samuel de Champlain founds Quebec as the capital of New France
Colbert establishes the French East India Company
Treaty of Paris cedes Canada and lands east of the Mississippi to Britain
France invades Algiers, beginning the second colonial empire
The Viet Minh force the surrender of the French garrison at Dien Bien Phu
Fourteen sub-Saharan colonies and trust territories become independent
The Evian Accords bring Algerian independence after eight years of war
